findings.title: withdraw() locks stakers with zero bonus when the registry skips straight to PRODUCTION, never passing through UNDER_ATTACK
findings.root_cause: withdraw() only permits exit in NOT_DEPLOYED/NEW_DEPLOYMENT/ATTACK_REQUESTED, assuming the registry always passes through UNDER_ATTACK; a jump to PRODUCTION closes the exit while riskWindowStart stays 0, so stakers are locked and earn no bonus.

findings.title: The recovery beneficiary can mint the CORRUPTED verdict its pool sweeps on, past the independent moderator
findings.root_cause: The factory forces sponsor = agreement owner = recovery beneficiary, and in the Safe Harbor integration that owner is also the attackModerator; it can markCorrupted, wait out the grace period and let anyone finalise a bad-faith CORRUPTED that sweeps the pool to its own recovery address, bypassing the outcome moderator.

findings.title: The moderator grace can expire before CORRUPTED exists, letting anyone finalize the pool before the moderator gets a protected chance to classify it
findings.root_cause: MODERATOR_CORRUPTED_GRACE counts from pool expiry rather than from when CORRUPTED first exists; if the agreement stays UNDER_ATTACK past the grace, the permissionless claimExpired fallback can finalise bad-faith CORRUPTED (latching claimsStarted) the moment it appears, before the moderator can classify it.
